work_completed: Sandbox check (step 0): (a) the write to `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/.sandbox-trial-DAEO-9nys` failed as it should (OSError, Errno 30, read-only file system). (b) `git hash-object -w --stdin` worked (1ae28402…) and `git update-index --refresh` worked (exit 0). `GOV_ROLE`=engineer, `GOV_TICKET`=DAEO-9nys; the top level is `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-67` on branch `w2/W2-67`. The change, in words: a run of this repository's suites now takes its shared `flock` on `.lock` as soon as pytest makes its base folder. It does this by wrapping the factory's `getbasetemp` in a `pytest_sessionstart(tryfirst)` hook in the controlling process, never in an xdist worker and never under a given `--basetemp`. This replaces the earlier `pytest_runtestloop` and `pytest_runtest_setup` hooks, which took the lock only after the first test's setup. While holding the lock, the run writes a `.lock-held` mark next to it. The end-of-run sweep (still past pytest's retention of three, same policies) now treats a run as over in exactly three cases: there is no `.lock`; or the sweep can lock `.lock` exclusively and `.lock-held` is there, which means the run that held it is gone, whatever its pid or namespace; or the `.lock` names a pid at or above `/proc/sys/kernel/pid_max`. Every other folder is kept, whatever its pid. The `os.kill` check is gone, because a pid cannot show liveness across PID namespaces. The `--basetemp` refusal is unchanged and still refuses.

After, all three files gave 37 passed, 0 failed: the 9 live-run cases (close-runner, foreign-project and suite-in-setup under none, all and failed) and the 2 killed same-pid cases now pass, and the cases that were green stay green. `tests/unit/guard/` (`-n auto`): 1054 passed. `tests/acceptance/W1-27/test_w2_67_copies.py` (`-n 2 --dist loadfile`): 6 passed. `tests/acceptance/W1-28` (`-n 2`): 151 passed. `tests/unit/close/` (`-n auto`): 386 passed, run twice. Every run was given `-o tmp_path_retention_policy=failed`; no run used `--basetemp` or `-x`.
discoveries: `tests/unit/close/test_run_and_record.py::test_a_run_over_the_time_limit_is_a_finding_not_an_error` starts a nested project run with `-n 2`. That run's controlling process makes a base folder, and `gov close`'s `_started` then ends it with `os.killpg(..., SIGKILL)` (`src/gov/close/command.py:912`). Its `.lock` stays behind with a dead pid and no `.lock-held` mark, because nested runs never load this conftest. I saw `pytest-5` (lock 5894) after the first close run and `pytest-37` (lock 3910) after the second, so each run leaves one. The head removed these through `os.kill`. The new rule must keep them, because the live close-runner case needs exactly that folder shape (a `.lock`, no mark, a pid the sweep cannot see) to be kept. I also tried `gov retrieve` once, for prior context on the sweep, the flock and PID namespaces; it answered FACET_UNAVAILABLE (lexical and semantic both stale), so I read the named files instead. Read refusals met: 0.
risks: (1) A run that includes `tests/unit/close` now leaves one extra base folder (2 inodes) per run until pytest's three-day rule removes it. Within three days these add up, so such a run can end with more than 3 base folders, which goes against KPI 4's "at most three" (see the package). (2) A killed run in the instant between pytest creating `.lock` and the flock being taken has no mark, so it is kept until the three-day rule. (3) The `getbasetemp` wrapper is an instance attribute on pytest's private `TempPathFactory`; a future pytest that called the class method directly would skip the hold, and the 9 live-run cases would catch that. (4) If `/proc/sys/kernel/pid_max` is lower in the sweep's namespace than in another one, the pid rule could remove a folder too early; there is no sign of that on this machine (pid_max 4194304).
lessons: Across PID namespaces a pid can neither show a run is alive nor show it is dead. The only proof is a flock held on the shared file plus a mark written while holding it: if the sweep holds the lock exclusively and the mark is there, the run that held it is gone. The mark check must happen while the sweep holds the exclusive lock.
proposed_decisions: Package P1, killed nested runs' base folders. Question: who removes the base folder of a nested run that `gov close`'s time limit kills with SIGKILL, now that the sweep keeps every folder that has no mark? Why now: every run of `tests/unit/close` leaves one, so a full run can leave more than 3 base folders (KPI 4, DEC-898). Options: (A) in the round-2 file `tests/unit/close/test_run_and_record.py`, the time-limit case sets `TMPDIR` to its own `tmp_path` with monkeypatch, so the killed run's base folder goes away with `tmp_path`. One line; easy to undo; it disturbs no nested run's behaviour. (B) in `src/gov/close/command.py`, start nested runs with a temp folder of their own per run, removed after the run. This changes `src/` in another scope and costs more; it would also cover real closes that hit the time limit. (C) Re-baseline KPI 4 so that "at most three" excludes folders whose run cannot be shown to be over, which pytest removes after three days; no code. Recommendation: A now, inside round 2, and B considered later for real closes. Confidence: medium-high.
unresolved: P1. Also left in TMPDIR for now: two markerless leftover folders from the close runs (`pytest-5`, `pytest-37`, 2 inodes each).
recommended_next_action: The ticket lead decides P1 (recommendation A in round 2's `tests/unit/close`), then runs the W1-07/W1-25/W1-26/W1-27 folders and the full-run base-folder count.
